title: Replace Cash Advances With CashBook and Cut Finance Work by Up to 80%
summary: Need an alternative to employee cash advances? CashBook UPI wallets replace cash and travel advances, with a bill on every payment and nothing to settle.
body_markdown:
**First, what we mean.** A cash advance is money a company hands to staff before they spend on company work: a trip, a site visit, a delivery route. It isn't a salary advance or an early wage.


**The short answer:** To replace cash advances, give each employee a company-funded UPI wallet. With CashBook, you top it up before or during the work, staff pay by UPI, and every payment arrives with its bill. Nobody chases bills afterwards, and there's no leftover cash to settle. That's the part of finance work that disappears.

## The short version


-


**The work starts after the money is spent.** Tracking, chasing bills, settling balances and re-typing entries all happen once the cash has gone.


-


**A wallet moves that work to the moment of payment,** where it takes seconds instead of weeks.


-


**Customers report up to 80% less work.** YoloBus cut its manual finance work by that much, and Zingbus now closes its month in a day instead of a week.


-


**Late bills can cost you GST credit.** A bill that comes back weeks later, or in an employee's name, often can't be used.


-


**Big cash payments can cost you the deduction.** India's income tax rules disallow cash payments above ₹10,000 to one person in a day.


## Where the finance work goes


A cash advance creates finance work after the money is spent. A wallet moves that work to the moment of payment.


In words: with a cash advance, finance hands out cash, staff spend with no record, finance chases bills for weeks, settles the leftover balance, then re-types everything into the books. With a CashBook wallet, finance tops up the wallet, staff pay by UPI with the bill attached, and entries sync to the books. Chasing bills and settling cash don't happen at all.

## What are the alternatives to employee cash advances?


The main alternative to employee cash advances is a company-funded UPI wallet, such as CashBook. Instead of handing over cash before the work, the company tops up each employee's wallet, and staff pay vendors directly by UPI with the bill attached to each payment.


Two other options come up often. Both remove the cash but keep most of the work:


-


**Reimbursement.** Staff pay from their own pocket and claim it back later. The company stops handing out cash, but its employees now fund the work, and finance still waits for bills. Before switching, YoloBus drivers paid tolls, repairs and meals from their own pockets, which delayed their reimbursements.


-


**Bank transfer to a personal account.** Faster than cash, but the money mixes with the employee's own, with no limits and no record of who was paid. In Zingbus's words from its case study: cash advances "dropped into personal accounts".


Only the wallet keeps the company's money separate until the moment it's spent, and creates the record at that moment.


If you're weighing corporate cards as well, we compare them in[Corporate Credit Card Alternative? Pay at 88 Crore UPI QR Codes With CashBook](https://cashbook.in/blogs/corporate-credit-card-alternative) .


## Why do cash advances create so much finance work?


Because the record is created after the money is spent, not when it's spent. Every advance turns into a small project for finance:


1.


**Track who holds what.** Each advance is an open balance against a person until someone settles it.


2.


**Chase the bills.** At RDash, bills used to come in "days or even weeks after the expense was made".


3.


**Check each bill.** Is it a proper tax invoice? Is it in the company's name? Was it for work?


4.


**Settle the balance.** Recover the unspent cash, or pay back the person who overspent.


5.


**Re-type it into the books.** Someone enters every bill into the accounts by hand.


Two rules make late or cash-paid bills more expensive than they look.


### Late bills can cost you GST credit


A business can claim[input tax credit](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/acts/2017_CGST_act/active/chapter5/section16_v1.00.html) only against a proper tax invoice issued to it, with its GSTIN on it. A hotel or vendor bill made out in an employee's name, or lost for three weeks, usually means that credit is gone. The later a bill comes back, the harder it is to get the vendor to reissue it.


### Big cash payments can cost you the deduction


[India's income tax rules](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/what-is-the-provision-of-section-40a-3-) don't let a business deduct a cash payment of more than ₹10,000 to one person in a day (₹35,000 for payments to transporters), apart from a few listed exceptions. An employee paying a supplier in cash out of an advance can cross that line without anyone noticing until the audit.


### Finance is always looking backwards


K2 Cranes & Components put it plainly in its case study: "When field spend happens in cash, finance is always looking backwards."


*"We had visibility only after the cash was gone and often weeks later."* Yagyarth, HR Manager, Zingbus

## How do field staff pay without a cash advance?


Field staff pay from a company-funded UPI wallet on their own phone. It's topped up as the work needs it, not handed over as one lump sum at the start of the month. In October 2026, UPI handled about 82 crore payments a day, according to[NPCI](https://www.npci.org.in/product/upi) , so the fuel pump, the mechanic and the roadside dhaba will almost always take UPI.


Picture a service engineer whose van needs a new tyre at 7 pm, 200 km from the office. The mechanic has a QR code on the wall. With an advance, the engineer hopes enough cash is left, or pays from their own UPI app and claims it later. With a CashBook wallet, they scan, pay with company money and photograph the bill, and finance sees it straight away.

## Frequently asked questions


### Is a cash advance the same as a salary advance?


No. A salary advance is part of an employee's pay given early. A cash advance, or travel advance, is company money given for work spending, which the employee has to account for. CashBook wallets replace cash advances, not salary advances.


### What is the best alternative to employee cash advances?


A company-funded UPI wallet like CashBook. The company tops up each employee's wallet, staff pay by UPI within set limits, and every payment carries its bill. There's nothing to settle after the work.


### What's the best app for managing travel advances in India?


One that removes the advance. CashBook gives each traveller a company-funded UPI wallet that head office tops up before or during the trip, with spending limits, a bill photo on every payment and nothing to settle afterwards.


### How do you settle an employee advance?


With a cash advance, finance collects the bills, recovers unspent cash or repays any overspend, then enters everything into the books. With a CashBook wallet there's no settlement step: each payment is recorded with its bill when it's made, and unspent money stays in the wallet as company money.


### How can finance track employee advances?


Give each employee a wallet instead of an advance. Each wallet shows a live balance and every payment with its bill, so finance sees spending as it happens, not when the bills come back.


### Can staff get more money in the middle of a trip?


Yes. Head office can top up a wallet in seconds, wherever the employee is.


### What happens to money left over after a trip?


It stays in the employee's wallet as company money for the next job. There's no cash to collect. If the person leaves, you freeze the wallet.


### Do staff still need to keep bills?


Yes, but they add a photo with each payment instead of collecting paper for weeks. Ask vendors for bills in the company's name with its GSTIN, so you can claim GST input credit.


### Can wallets pay vendors who don't have a QR code?


Yes. Staff can pay any UPI ID as well as any UPI QR code.


### Does every employee need a smartphone?


Yes. Each person who spends needs the CashBook app on their own phone.


### How does CashBook keep company money safe?


Money leaves the master wallet only after an OTP goes to your Payment Admin. Every wallet has its own limits, and any wallet can be frozen in seconds. CashBook's payments product has been reviewed by NPCI and audited by a CERT-In empanelled auditor.
